topic: How would the 0.25 dB passband loss affect link budget margins in low-noise satellite receiver frontends?
consensus_response: The 0.25 dB passband loss reduces SNR, impacting link margins and reliability. It interacts with non-linear effects in amplifiers, exacerbating distortion, and affects phase noise tolerance, degrading demodulation performance. Polarization mismatch further compounds signal degradation, increasing bit error rates and service disruptions.
reference_context: SatCom systems rely on precise link budgets, considering factors like channel gain, noise temperature, and antenna efficiency to maintain reliability.
